overview: Government Grants Eligibility Screening addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in government and public sector operations. The first proof of value uses grant policy, applicant declarations and required evidence. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is applications with complete eligibility evidence, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: grant policy, applicant declarations and required evidence; define applications with complete eligibility evidence and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Government CIO / Agency Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for applications with complete eligibility evidence
